text:
(L-R) Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje are due to face off in the main event of UFC Freedom 250 at the White House on Sunday

UFC Freedom 250 headliners Ilia Topuria and Justin Gaethje have added another layer of chaos to their fight this weekend by taking several vicious swipes at each other on social media.

Topuria, 29, and Gaethje, 37, will contest the main event on the South Lawn of the White House on Sunday, which happens to be a UFC Lightweight Championship title unification bout between the current champion (Topuria) and the current two-time interim champion (Gaethje).

Ahead of the fight, Topuria has already offered some friendly fire toward Gaethje by promising U.S. President Donald Trump that their bout will be "over quickly", believing it will end "similarly" to his Oliveira fight when he knocked his Brazilian opponent out in the first round 12 months ago.

Things between the Georgian-Spanish mixed martial artist and the American, however, have quickly reached boiling point over the past few days.

Last week, a clip emerged online showing Gaethje's father dismissing his son's upcoming bout with Topuria, claiming he is just fighting "another little short guy" and that, even though it is the biggest fight of his life, it's nothing he hasn't handled before.

The video soon made its way to Topuria, who responded in a post on X by saying that he's "heard this story before" and just like with his previous fights, the outcome will be the same, signing off with: "Your son already knows who I am. On June 14th, you will too. 18-0 PAPA."

Speaking with Fox Australia shortly after, Gaethje was asked about Topuria's trademark habit of presenting his opponents with a rose after defeating them, following a video in which the German-born fighter places a special white rose at the base of a Gaethje mural, and what followed was a personal attack that marked the beginning of their nasty, bitter feud.

Topuria is renowned for handing his opponents a rose once he has defeated them, something Gaethje has made clear he is not a fan of(Image: Getty Images)

"All that guy is is a gimmick," Gaethje said. "He calls himself the king. He thinks he's a God. What an annoying little b------. I couldn't imagine being in a room with him for 30 minutes, listening to him talk about himself."

"And I can say this: I would leave him," Gaethje added, referencing Topuria's recent divorce from his wife, Giorgina Uzcategui. "That's all I'm saying. I would leave him. No way I would put up with his s---."

That proved to be a big mistake from Gaethje, as Topuria only used it as ammunition to fire back an even sterner warning than before about what he will do to the American inside the octagon.

"Take this, Justin [shows middle finger]," Topuria said in the first episode of UFC Freedom 250 Embedded this week. "Actually, I thought he was a great guy. But since he crossed the personal line, he's not going to have my respect; he's not going to have my team's respect.

Gaethje left Topuria enraged after making reference to his recent split from his ex-wife

"All I'm going to need is two minutes in the octagon with you, and I'm going to put you to sleep in front of your whole family, your country, in front of everyone."

Topuria, however, wasn't done there, as he then followed up with another response to Gaethje's comments in a post on X on Monday, stating: "Justin crossed a line.

"What happened between my ex-wife and me is our business. We may no longer be together, but she is the mother of my daughter. To everyone insulting her or speaking about things they know nothing about: show some respect.

"You don't have to respect our relationship. But respecting someone's mother should be one of the most basic codes in life. Be better."

Gaethje soon caught wind of the post and viciously responded: "Proving my point. Insufferable little b---- boy. Never said a thing about your wife. You want to speak words to my father then act like I crossed some line. We already fighting buddy."

Within half an hour, Topuria was back with a further warning to Gaethje, writing: "You should've kept your father out of this. He was the one calling me a short guy and saying you'd smash me, all while holding a beer in his hand.

"Then you started talking about my divorce and telling the world you wouldn't want to be my roommate. Idiot. First, we're fighting, not dating. Second, I'm not looking for a roommate.

"When I put you to sleep and you're lying there next to the rose, I'll look at your father and ask him one simple question: Who's the short one now? I'm gonna break you Justin."
